name: newsman
summary: Run opt-in email on your own Cloudflare account with Rust and Amazon SES. Every web action is also a tool on the HTTP MCP server.

settings.label: Workspace display name
settings.help: Display this name in the operator console and recipient-facing signup flow.

settings.label: Public application origin
settings.help: Use the canonical HTTPS origin of your installation for signup, consent and remote client access.

settings.label: Reporting time zone
settings.help: Use an IANA time zone to present operator-selected send times and reporting windows.

settings.label: Optional archive handoff delay in days
settings.help: Use a nonnegative whole number up to 365 when a message has a web release. Standalone email needs no archive or delay.

settings.label: Amazon SES region
settings.help: Select the AWS region of your verified sender, production sending account and feedback configuration.

files.about: Requirements for a self-hosted opt-in email application with complete HTTP MCP access.
Machine-readable registry and schemas for operator and recipient HTTP MCP tools and web actions.
Client connection, examples, permissions, file transfer and web/MCP parity checks.
Rust identity and OAuth flow, the operator allowlist, delegated scopes and recipient proofs.
Cloudflare deployment, SES feedback, recipient delivery boundaries, costs and recovery.
Optional suppression-first migration from beehiiv or another list manager, with a reconciliation exercise.
Checks for the Rust reference implementation, remote MCP operation and standalone sending.
Public signup behavior, static REA evidence and independent implementation choices.

changelog.note: Publications can brand reader confirmation pages and send the current private edition once after first confirmation. Dated full-audience campaigns supply the edition for the week. A publisher can pin an edition delivered by a previous provider during migration.
The publication name appears in the From header of newsletters, confirmations, reminders and operator emails. Previews and send plans show the same display name and sender address.

Pending readers can receive one automatic confirmation reminder after 48 hours. A publication can connect its signup form, acknowledge durable first confirmations and honor later opt-outs from its previous provider.
Browser consent returns to the exact registered connector callback through a separate GET. Connectors can redirect to their canonical host, and a spent consent form explains how to reconnect.
Browser sign-in, sign-out and the hosted signup form preserve the Origin required for CSRF checks. OAuth consent returns operators to their registered connector callback after approval or denial.
Hosted MCP clients can connect using trusted OAuth client metadata, exact callbacks and PKCE. Streamable HTTP negotiates three protocol revisions and describes the scopes required by each tool.
Concurrent signed SES notifications retry their database writes. Persistent contention returns HTTP 503 so SNS can redeliver pending feedback.
Operators can sign in with verified inbox codes. The deployment allowlist applies to both MCP resources. A recipient-restricted pilot supports one-click proofs and short-lived AWS role credentials.
The console uses self-hosted Geist Sans for the wordmark, headings and counters. The gallery shows the publishing desk on desktop and mobile, the message editor and HTTP MCP connections.
General-purpose opt-in email publishing, independent send times, optional web handoff, MIT-licensed Rust reference implementation, full remote MCP access and screenshots of the running console.
Initial specification for self-hosted email delivery with Cloudflare, Amazon SES and HTTP MCP.
